title: Lick Observatory Main Building, Mount Hamilton
geometryBasis: The named Main Building’s 63 mapped corners and independent fitted circles control both domes, connecting hall and east range. The native telescope pin is inside the south drum. Two cleared photographs document the west entrance and the domes.
sectionBasis: The period handbook records the south dome at about 75 feet in diameter, a smaller 25-foot north telescope dome, and a 191-foot connecting hall. The larger rotating cap follows the published diameter. The smaller cap and visible drums use the mapped circular footprints and exterior proportions. Exterior heights, roof sections, east range details and threshold grade are estimates.
limitations: The 2019 exterior interpretation covers the Main Building, both attached domes and the east range. It depicts the south observing shutter closed.
The historic handbook and mapped footprint constrain the main dimensions. East-range fenestration, elevations, roof profiles and material wear are estimated.
The original summit terrain remains unchanged. The exposed foundation follows an approximate local grade.
